html:
The world order is significantly shaped today by the looming US and Israeli elections, both explicitly noted to have global consequences, driving geopolitical maneuvering particularly across the Middle East. These electoral stakes unfold amidst a dramatic political comeback in Brazil and escalating regional security crises.

Great-Power Dynamics: Upcoming US midterms see US President Donald Trump offer a $1 million reward for voter fraud conviction tips, following a ruling that the Trump administration illegally fired Maurene Comey. In an unexpected development for a reliably red state, Republican David Beasley and Democrat Jim Hodges issued a rare joint endorsement for Democrat Annie Andrews in a South Carolina Senate race. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy criticized Trump’s defense secretary Pete Hegseth for delaying supplies of Patriot interceptor missiles. In Europe, Serbia's student-backed movement secured a historic parliamentary election victory, ending the decade-long dominance of a Moscow-backed populist leader. Meanwhile, China's closed-door plenum began as Xi seeks stronger party discipline ahead of an expected fourth term.

Middle East Diplomacy & Conflict: A quadrilateral meeting in Tehran involving Iran, Pakistan, Turkey, and Saudi Arabia aimed to de-escalate tensions between Iran and the U.S. and in Yemen, with Iran's president signaling openness to regional cooperation. This diplomatic push contrasts with reports that the U.S. military is ready for a large-scale attack on Iran within 96 hours of an order from Trump, who has warned Iran of "death problems" should it obtain a nuclear weapon. Separately, Egypt's parliament authorized Sisi to send military support to Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks escalated, prompting the U.S. to order non-emergency staff to leave Saudi Arabia.

Israeli-Palestinian Tensions: A UN inquiry found that Israel has committed genocide in Gaza after a truce, as well as war crimes and crimes against humanity in the Occupied Palestinian Territory. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed a large-scale West Bank operation, beginning with the expulsion of Palestinians in Hebron, an action that the UN cites for "ethnic cleansing" concerns. Israel launched major West Bank raids after two soldiers were killed. Ahead of this week's Israeli elections, international delegates, including British politicians, were barred from entering the West Bank.

Global Economy & Technology: The artificial intelligence company Anthropic warned of "catastrophic risk" to humankind ahead of its blockbuster share listing, underscoring both the promise and peril of the burgeoning AI sector. Economically, Iran's economy is reportedly "collapsing" as the U.S. Treasury tightens its financial vise, with one analyst predicting a more than 25% contraction. Separately, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's plan to bypass sanctions using cryptocurrency has drawn criticism, with opponents warning of potential "diplomatic and financial isolation."

Latin America & Africa Political Shifts: In a dramatic Brazil election comeback, incumbent president Lula secured a fourth term, defeating right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro, who was subsequently ordered to surrender his passports amid reference to a money-laundering case. In Venezuela, opposition leader María Corina Machado returned after months in exile. In Africa, Algeria is set to send troops to Niger to protect energy facilities, marking its first foreign deployment since 1973, while more than 60 Christians were reportedly killed in an Ethiopia 'massacre'.
